reviews.outlet: StraySpark blog: Claude Code vs Cursor vs Windsurf for Unreal Engine (2026)
reviews.author: StraySpark (game studio; no individual named)
reviews.summary: Months of UE5 C++ use with all three tools. Claude Code was the main recommendation for MCP-driven editor automation and multi-file refactors (first-try compile in 7 of 10 runs of an inventory-component refactor). Downsides: no built-in IntelliSense, slower startup and higher daily token cost.
reviews.note: StraySpark sells an Unreal MCP Server that works with these tools, so it may favour MCP-heavy workflows. No affiliate links found.

reviews.outlet: StraySpark blog: Claude Code vs Cursor vs Windsurf for Unreal Engine (2026)

caveats: 1) The shared WebSearch budget (200 per session) ran out partway through. Later work used WebFetch on known URLs only, so community sampling for general tools (Unity/Unreal/Godot forums, Hacker News) is thin. Reddit/X were skipped as instructed. 2) Blocked or unreadable: tbench.ai (JS-rendered; used Snorkel-hosted boards credited by the TB maintainers), arena.ai/LMArena WebDev (403, no model-level data recorded), G2/Capterra/Fab (403), Ars Technica (blocked; used GIGAZINE summary), the Creative Bloq and MSN Unity AI pieces (empty), forum.godotengine.org tag pages (404), the AA leaderboard table (rows read from the BenchLM mirror plus AA comparison pages). 3) Benchmarks: the most decision-relevant product-level boards are Terminal-Bench 4.0, AA Coding Agent Index v2.0 and the two game-engine benchmarks (GameDevBench for Godot, GameEngineBench for UE5 C++). Only Claude Code and Codex appear on them. Cursor appears only on the archived Terminal-Bench 2.1. Copilot, Windsurf/Devin Desktop and the three engine-integrated tools have no product benchmark. Leaderboards list several effort settings per product, and percentiles here use the best current-model row. Some board rows may be lab-submitted. 4) Excluded or not scored: GameCraft-Bench (Tencent co-authored, includes Tencent's Code Buddy), the SWE-bench Pro public board (Scale; model-only, stale models), Vals TB 2.0 (June 2026, model-only, superseded), aiconjured.com (claims thousands of reviews per tool with no source; looks unreliable), Quickmatch/dev.to (not hands-on, affiliate links), Summer Engine and Ziva blogs (competing Godot AI vendors), the Stack Overflow 2026 AI page (percentages for Claude Code 66% and Copilot 59% without a clear metric). 5) Review-site skews: Product Hunt ratings are near 5.0 for every coding tool; Trustpilot for Cursor and Windsurf is billing-dominated. VS Code Marketplace star averages couldn't be read exactly, so they're not scored. 6) I ran one curl to inspect gamedevbench.com (it's a placeholder page). All other access was via WebSearch/WebFetch. 7) Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (windsurf.com redirects to devin.ai/desktop).
